rows.notes: Token resolution stays as one indexed token-hash lookup plus invitation join before the open audit write.
Active-token uniqueness is enforced by a partial unique index and queried directly by invitation id.
Pending-invite account lookup uses the email/lifecycle/created-at index and stays explicit in the D1 repository.
Accept replay checks natural membership uniqueness before reporting already_member without duplicate side effects.

d1RewriteStrategy.typeStrategy: Typed D1 repository return models should mirror the current invitation terminal-state union while SQLite CHECK constraints enforce lifecycle, scope, role, and token uniqueness until a broader D1 type-generation strategy lands.

productionProofRequirements: Keep the hosted Worker+D1 collaboration invitation proof current after invite route, token, membership, audit, or auth changes.
Run token issue, delivery, resolve, wrong-account, revoked, expired, replay, accept-by-token, accept-by-id, rollback, and idempotency tests inside the Worker runtime when those paths change.
Capture hosted Worker+D1 query count, p95 duration, rows read/written, and failure telemetry for invite entry GET/POST and pending-invite acceptance paths.
Run a provider-backed D1 export/restore rehearsal for invitation tokens, memberships, and audit rows before treating D1 as the source of truth.
note: Local-only D1 collaboration-invitation domain proof. It uses sanitized temporary SQLite tables to model token issue/revoke-existing, delivery audit, invite resolution, revoked/expired/used terminal states, wrong-account denial, token and by-id acceptance, replay handling, rollback, idempotency, query-budget, index-plan, and export/restore behavior. It does not read env files, call provider APIs, create hosted D1 databases, deploy Workers, change DNS, bill, or by itself prove the full hosted two-client in-app collaboration UI journey.
